entities.summary: A United States Army captain who took control at Mariposa during the 2077 crisis, led the survivors to Lost Hills and became the founding leader of the Brotherhood of Steel.
entities.description: Roger Maxson's surviving logs provide an unusually detailed first-person chronology of the Mariposa crisis. They show a security officer struggling to control a mutiny, taking part in the killing of the research staff, breaking with the United States and then trying to build a durable post-War institution from the people under his command.

articleSections.title: Pre-War service and Mariposa assignment
paragraphs: Maxson was a captain in the United States Army, service number 072389. At Mariposa he served beneath Colonel Robert Spindel as the security detachment's second-ranking officer. The soldiers guarded a highly classified research programme but were not initially told what the scientists were doing inside the base.

That arrangement matters because Maxson did not arrive as an ideological opponent of the government. His break developed inside a military chain of command that had concealed the use of human test subjects from the personnel ordered to protect it.

articleSections.title: Discovery of the FEV experiments
paragraphs: By 10 October 2077, the security personnel had discovered that the programme was experimenting on military prisoners. Maxson's diary records Spindel withdrawing into his office while the soldiers demanded action. Maxson tried to prevent an immediate lynching and ordered interrogations instead.

The attempt at legal control collapsed almost at once. On 13 October Maxson killed chief scientist Robert Anderson during an interrogation. Spindel died by suicide on 15 October, leaving Maxson as the effective commander. By 18 October the interrogations were ending in executions, and Maxson's own account had stopped presenting them as a defensible judicial process.

articleSections.title: Break with the United States
paragraphs: On 20 October, Maxson used the base radio to declare that his command had seceded from the United States. He appears to have expected the declaration to force a response from higher authority. None came. His entry of 22 October treats the silence as evidence that a wider catastrophe was imminent.

This was a rebellion before it was the Brotherhood of Steel. Maxson was still using Army rank and procedure, even as he rejected federal command. The distinction helps explain why the archive treats the Mariposa mutiny, the exodus and the later Brotherhood proclamation as related but separate developments.

articleSections.title: The Great War at Mariposa
paragraphs: The bombs fell on 23 October while the remaining prisoners were still being questioned. Mariposa retained contact long enough for Maxson to infer that the original West Tek research site had been struck, but the base itself escaped the immediate blast. Families had already been moved inside, an action later records credit with saving them.

The following days were practical and morally unsettled. Sergeant Platner tested the outside atmosphere in power armour on 25 October. On 26 October the soldiers buried the scientists, and Maxson wrote that he had finally accepted their claim that the experiments had been authorised by the government.

articleSections.title: Exodus to Lost Hills
paragraphs: Maxson's formal order of 24 October directed military personnel and their families to leave for the Lost Hills security bunker. His diary records the actual departure on 27 October. The refugees carried equipment judged necessary for survival and left Mariposa's civilian personnel behind pending lawful orders that could no longer arrive.

The journey converted a mutinous garrison into a displaced community. Later Brotherhood records remember Maxson as the deliverer who brought the survivors to the bunker. They also preserve the cost: the civilian column suffered casualties, including Maxson's wife, while at least one group under Sergeant Dennis Allen broke away to search the ruined West Tek site.

articleSections.title: From captain to founding elder
paragraphs: At Lost Hills, Maxson's survivors secured a permanent base and remained in contact with distant military survivors where communications allowed. Fallout 76 records his contact with Lieutenant Elizabeth Taggerdy in Appalachia and show the Brotherhood identity developing as a deliberate break from the failed institutions of the pre-War state.

Maxson argued that names, ranks and traditions could give traumatised survivors a shared identity while insulating them from any returning politician or general who might repeat the old cycle. The Brotherhood proclamation and the later preservation directive joined two ideas: disciplined mutual purpose, and the recovery of knowledge needed for a future civilisation.

articleSections.title: Legacy and limits of the record
paragraphs: A later Maxson archive at the Citadel says that Roger Maxson served as the first High Elder, created the orders of Paladins, Knights and Scribes, and died of cancer in 2135. His descendants continued to lead the western Brotherhood, but later chapters interpreted the founding mission in markedly different ways.

Maxson's diary is unusually candid but still personal testimony. It establishes what he saw, did and believed; it does not turn every judgement in the diary into objective fact. In particular, the archive does not sanitise his responsibility for the executions at Mariposa simply because later Brotherhood tradition revered him.

entities.summary: Roger Maxson's son and a later leader of the Brotherhood of Steel.
The unnamed Vault 13 resident sent to recover a water chip, tasked with ending the mutant threat and exiled after defeating the Unity.
entities.description: Fallout leaves the Vault Dweller's personal name, sex, route and exact completion dates open. The record therefore follows mission structure and supported relationships rather than inventing a single playthrough.

articleSections.title: A resident of Vault 13
paragraphs: The protagonist begins as a member of a sealed community that has remained underground for roughly eighty years. The game supplies no canonical personal name and allows the player to define sex, abilities and conduct.
That openness is part of the lore model: 'Vault Dweller' is a role and descriptive title, not evidence for a fixed biography imported from one playthrough.

articleSections.title: The water-chip mission
paragraphs: The Overseer sends the Dweller toward Vault 15 after Vault 13's purification controller fails. The eventual replacement comes through the water system beneath Necropolis, but the route, detours and completion date vary.
Returning the chip resolves the immediate mechanical crisis and triggers a second mission rather than ending the journey.

articleSections.title: Conflict with Unity
paragraphs: The successful route eliminates both Mariposa's production vats and the Master beneath the Cathedral. Fallout permits either order and several methods, so the archive records common outcomes without selecting a canonical tactical path.

articleSections.title: Return and exile
paragraphs: The Overseer praises the returning hero but refuses readmission, arguing that younger Vault residents would imitate the Dweller and leave. The decision turns the saviour of Vault 13 into an exile in order to preserve the Vault's closed political order.
The player may leave or kill the Overseer. Exile is shared by both final variants; the Overseer's survival is conditional.

entities.summary: A leader of Shady Sands and father of Tandi.
A Shady Sands resident who became a formative political leader of the New California Republic.
A chemist associated with the Mordino family who claimed responsibility for creating Jet.
entities.description: Myron's account is retained as a source statement. Other released material complicates a simple post-War origin for Jet, so the archive does not silently promote his claim into settled world fact.

entities.summary: The founder and autocratic leader of Caesar's Legion in the Mojave conflict.
A founding Legion commander who led its forces during the First Battle of Hoover Dam.
The pre-War industrialist whose systems preserved Las Vegas and who later ruled New Vegas from the Lucky 38.
President of the Enclave during its conflict with the Chosen One in 2242.
A post-War military order founded by Roger Maxson's followers, organised around disciplined service and the preservation and control of dangerous technology.
entities.description: The Brotherhood did not appear fully formed on the day of the Great War. It developed from the Mariposa security detachment and its families after their rebellion, exodus and settlement at Lost Hills, then acquired a new name, hierarchy and preservation mission during the first post-War years.

articleSections.title: Origins at Mariposa
paragraphs: The Brotherhood's institutional ancestry begins with a United States Army security unit at Mariposa Military Base. The unit rebelled after discovering FEV experimentation on prisoners, lost its commanding officer during the crisis and followed Captain Roger Maxson out of the base after the Great War.

Calling this group the Brotherhood immediately would erase a documented transition. Maxson's October 2077 records still use Army ranks and procedures. The later order emerged after the survivors reached Lost Hills and decided that returning to the old national chain of command would reproduce the failures they had just witnessed.

articleSections.title: A new name and identity
paragraphs: In the Brotherhood formation recording, Maxson rejects the idea that survival and shelter are enough. He proposes a new organisation able to preserve what was valuable in the old world without restoring the authorities that had driven it to destruction.

A private discussion with Elizabeth Taggerdy explains the medieval vocabulary. Maxson believed that repeated names could build identity and purpose. Knights and Scribes evoked people who had defended and transmitted knowledge after the collapse of Rome; Elder marked a new authority distinct from president, senator or general. The symbolism was therefore an institutional tool, not evidence that the early group had literally returned to medieval society.

articleSections.title: Lost Hills and the founding chapter
paragraphs: Lost Hills became the Brotherhood's headquarters and the physical centre of its founding chapter. The bunker protected families, workshops, archives and supplies, allowing the survivors to convert a refugee column into a permanent community.

By 2161 the site contained an elder council, military orders, technical workshops and a scribe establishment. Fallout presents this mature institution long after Maxson's founding generation, but Brotherhood histories retained the exodus as the event that made the bunker their home.

articleSections.title: Preservation as a mission
paragraphs: The strongest early statement of the preservation mission comes from Maxson's address to Appalachia. He argues that schematics, recordings, books and technical knowledge were disappearing faster than society could recover. Scribes were to preserve and extend that knowledge; Knights were to protect both the people and the archives that made rebuilding possible.

This early formulation is broader than simple weapons collection. It links technology recovery to the eventual return of civilisation and still speaks of helping other survivors. Later chapters narrowed, expanded or contested that mission, which is why the archive treats chapter policy as changing state rather than assuming one timeless Brotherhood ideology.

articleSections.title: Orders, leadership and chapters
paragraphs: The founding hierarchy divided responsibilities among Paladins, Knights and Scribes under elders. The orders created a durable vocabulary that geographically separated chapters continued to recognise even when their policies diverged.

Appalachia provides the earliest known remote adoption of the identity. Taggerdy's Thunder accepted Maxson's authority by long-distance communication and became a Brotherhood chapter without relocating to California. Later branches, including the Mojave chapter, demonstrate how the organisation could remain genealogically and institutionally connected to Lost Hills while operating with substantial local autonomy.

articleSections.title: Development after Maxson
paragraphs: The Brotherhood outlived its founder. The Citadel archive dates Roger Maxson's death to 2135 and identifies his son as his successor. By the time of Fallout in 2161, the order had become cautious about outsiders, technologically capable and governed by an elder council from Lost Hills.

The archive does not project every later doctrine backwards. Isolationism, recruitment policy, relations with civilian settlements and the meaning of technological stewardship changed across periods and chapters. Those differences are essential to understanding the Brotherhood as a historical organisation rather than a single fixed stereotype.

articleSections.title: What the sources establish
paragraphs: Fallout supplies the Mariposa diary, evacuation order, Lost Hills history and the mature 2161 organisation. Fallout 3's Citadel archive consolidates Maxson family and institutional history. Fallout 76 adds the founder's own recorded explanation for the Brotherhood name, ranks and preservation mission.

The exact moment at which the label Brotherhood of Steel became official is less secure than the sequence of events. The formation recording is not itself dated. The timeline therefore presents the founding as an approximate early post-War development rather than manufacturing a day and month.

articleSections.title: Lost Hills in 2161
paragraphs: By 2161 the Brotherhood is governed by elders under High Elder John Maxson. Rhombus leads military training, Vree represents scientific work, Talus handles Paladin matters and Cabbot meets outsiders at the entrance.
Scribes preserve and design, Knights manufacture and maintain, and Paladins protect the organisation. The Brotherhood trades for food and supplies while restricting access to its bunker.

articleSections.title: The mutant threat
paragraphs: John Maxson suspects an organised mutant army, but the council initially requires evidence. The Vault Dweller can supply proof and secure Paladin support against Unity targets.

articleSections.title: Contradictory ending branches
paragraphs: A favourable ending presents restrained aid, research and reintroduction of technology without direct rule. A hostile branch produces the Steel Plague, a techno-religious dictatorship.
The outcomes are explicitly mutually exclusive and should not be used as a timeless definition of the faction.

entities.summary: The pre-War military organisation in which Roger Maxson served.
The pre-War federal state whose institutions and conflicts shaped the world that preceded the Great War.
A secretive organisation descended from elements of the pre-War United States government.
The pre-War corporation responsible for the Vault programme.
A post-War republic founded from Shady Sands and expanded across parts of California and into the Mojave.
An expansionist autocracy formed from conquered tribes and led by Caesar.
A Brotherhood chapter based in the Mojave Wasteland, centred on Hidden Valley.
A Boneyard educational and humanitarian organisation founded by Nicole around peace, preserved knowledge and resistance to another cycle of war.
entities.description: The Followers combine teaching and medical aid with investigation of the Children; their survival and future influence are conditional in Fallout's endings.

articleSections.title: Formation and mission
paragraphs: Nicole formed the organisation after migration and violence killed her parents. The group preserves knowledge, teaches peace and tries to prevent another catastrophe.

articleSections.title: Investigation of the Children
paragraphs: Nicole suspects the Children after dissidents disappear. Laura infiltrates the Cathedral and reports concealed access used by Nightkin.

articleSections.title: Conditional outcomes
paragraphs: With support and without invasion, the Followers become an important Boneyard influence. In the invasion branch they are destroyed by mutant forces. Neither future is unconditional.

entities.summary: A tribal society descended from earlier Khan groups and active in the Mojave region.
The Master's coercive movement and army, using the Children as a public front and Mariposa to convert selected humans into super mutants.
entities.description: Unity combines an anti-war ideal of ending difference with forced conversion, planned sterilisation, killing of resisters and a search for uncontaminated Vault populations.

articleSections.title: Ideology and policy
paragraphs: The Master claims that a single mutant race can end the human divisions that caused nuclear war. Unity policy turns that premise into compulsory transformation and political domination.

articleSections.title: Children, army and command
paragraphs: The Children provide hospitals, missionaries and a public theology. Nightkin guard concealed functions, the Lieutenant commands Mariposa and the Master directs the whole project beneath the Cathedral.

articleSections.title: Captive and Vault search network
paragraphs: Scavenger teams abduct caravan travellers, assess their contamination and forward useful captives to Mariposa. Vault populations are especially valuable because low-radiation subjects tend to produce better mutants.

articleSections.title: Loss of the Master and vats
paragraphs: The successful route destroys both the Cathedral command centre and the Mariposa production vats. Ending narration says the surviving armies flee east after losing leader and reinforcement source.
The order of the two targets varies, so the archive models a shared strategic result rather than two simultaneous versions.

entities.summary: A pre-War government security bunker in California that sheltered the Mariposa exodus and became the headquarters and institutional home of the founding Brotherhood of Steel.
entities.description: Lost Hills is both a place and a turning point: it gave Maxson's refugees a defensible home from which a displaced Army unit could become a multi-generational order.

articleSections.title: A government security bunker
paragraphs: Lost Hills existed before the Great War as an underground government security installation. Maxson's evacuation order identifies it as the destination for Mariposa's military personnel and families, suggesting that the garrison knew of the site and considered it a viable refuge.

The exact real-world placement of the fictional bunker is not established with street-level precision. The map therefore uses a broad, explicitly inferred California browsing point rather than treating the game map as a GPS survey.

articleSections.title: Arrival of the exodus
paragraphs: Maxson's group left Mariposa on 27 October 2077. Brotherhood historical testimony remembers the survivors reaching the safety of the bunker and Maxson declaring it their new home. Later records place the arrival in November, but the primary Fallout material does not provide an exact arrival day.

The refugees included soldiers and their families, making Lost Hills a community as well as a military post. The journey's casualties and the separation of Dennis Allen's party reinforced the value of a secure permanent base.

articleSections.title: Institutional home of the Brotherhood
paragraphs: At Lost Hills, the survivors expanded and adapted the bunker into the headquarters of the new Brotherhood. The protected workshops and archives supported a division of labour between military and technical orders, while the settlement's isolation made it possible to preserve personnel and equipment across generations.

By 2161, Fallout depicts a substantial underground complex governed by a High Elder and council, with Knights, Paladins, Scribes and initiates occupying distinct roles. That mature organisation should not be assumed to have existed unchanged from the first weeks after arrival.

articleSections.title: Historical role and continuity
paragraphs: Lost Hills remained the symbolic centre of the western Brotherhood even after distant chapters developed. It connected the order's founding story, senior leadership and claim to institutional continuity.

The archive separates this durable place identity from changing political and organisational facts. The bunker can persist while its leadership, relations with neighbours and role within the wider Brotherhood change over time.

articleSections.title: The bunker in 2161
paragraphs: Fallout presents Lost Hills as a multi-level headquarters with entrance control, training, manufacturing, medical, library and council functions. Its internal geography expresses the division between military, technical and political work.

articleSections.title: Outsiders and initiation
paragraphs: The Brotherhood is cautious toward outsiders. Cabbot directs an applicant to the lethally irradiated Glow, echoing the earlier Dennis Allen expedition while turning retrieval into an initiation test.

entities.summary: A classified California military installation where the pre-War FEV programme moved into human experimentation and where Roger Maxson's security detachment rebelled in October 2077.
entities.description: Mariposa connects the FEV programme, the last days of the United States and the origins of the Brotherhood of Steel. Its history must distinguish the research facility, the security unit ordered to guard it and the later post-War uses of the site.

articleSections.title: Purpose and construction
paragraphs: Mariposa was built as a military installation for the advanced FEV programme. On 7 January 2077, Major Barnett ordered the West Tek research team to transfer its FEV work there. The surviving laboratory record objects to human trials, even while describing the intended subjects as volunteers.

The move separated the most sensitive work from the original West Tek facility and placed it behind military security. It also meant that the soldiers guarding the programme were physically close to experiments whose purpose had been withheld from them.

articleSections.title: Security detachment
paragraphs: Colonel Robert Spindel commanded the Mariposa security team, with Captain Roger Maxson as second in command. The unit included personnel such as Sergeant Platner and lived alongside military families attached to the garrison.

The security assignment gave the soldiers authority over the facility without giving them informed oversight of the research. That contradiction became decisive when they discovered that the test subjects were military prisoners.

articleSections.title: Human experimentation
paragraphs: The FEV programme had progressed from microbes and animals to human subjects by the time the Mariposa soldiers discovered it. Maxson's diary identifies the subjects as military prisoners and records the scientists' insistence that their orders came from the government.

The archive treats the scientists' claim of government authority as strongly supported by the surrounding programme records, but it preserves Maxson's first-person perspective separately. His eventual belief that they had been telling the truth does not erase the killings that occurred during the interrogations.

articleSections.title: The October 2077 rebellion
paragraphs: Between 10 and 20 October the garrison's command structure collapsed. Spindel withdrew and then died by suicide. Maxson killed Robert Anderson, the remaining interrogations became executions, and Maxson emerged as the soldiers' leader.

On 20 October he declared the command seceded from the United States. The base received no intervention before the Great War severed communications three days later. This sequence is unusually well dated because Maxson kept a near-daily record.

articleSections.title: The Great War and evacuation
paragraphs: Mariposa was not destroyed during the opening nuclear exchange. The garrison sheltered its families, assessed the outside atmosphere and prepared to leave. Maxson's written order sent military personnel and their families to Lost Hills, while directing civilian staff to remain pending lawful orders.
The group departed on 27 October after burying the executed scientists. Mariposa was left behind with Maxson's diary, which is later recoverable from the base's vats control computer.

articleSections.title: Later significance
paragraphs: Mariposa remained important after its original garrison left. Its FEV vats later became central to the Unity's super mutant programme, tying the Brotherhood's place of origin to the threat confronted by the Vault Dweller in the twenty-second century.

That later history is adjacent to, but distinct from, the production-quality cluster in this pass. The current record establishes the pre-War programme and 2077 rebellion while retaining links into FEV and the Unity for future deepening.

articleSections.title: Unity production centre in 2161
paragraphs: By 2161 Unity occupies Mariposa and uses the former research base as its principal conversion centre. The Lieutenant commands detention, interrogation and the FEV vats while field teams send screened captives for processing.
This later occupation extends the site's history without replacing the 2077 rebellion and exodus already documented by the archive.

articleSections.title: Destruction of mutant production
paragraphs: Neutralising the vats is required on the successful route because it removes Unity's ability to create new troops. The exact infiltration or combat method and its calendar date are player-dependent.

entities.summary: The isolated mountain Vault whose water-purification controller failure begins Fallout and whose population faces dehydration or Unity discovery in failure branches.
entities.description: Vault 13 is both a technological system and a closed society. Its survival depends on repair, secrecy and an Overseer willing to exile the person who preserved it.

articleSections.title: A closed mountain community
paragraphs: Vault residents describe a community that has remained below ground for about eighty years. Hydroponics, security, medical and technical roles support daily life, while unrest is treated as a threat to collective survival.
The Overseer's final decision shows that isolation is political as well as physical: contact with the outside can destabilise the social order even when it saves the population.

articleSections.title: Water-chip failure
paragraphs: The Vault's purification controller fails shortly before 5 December 2161. The Overseer says local workshops cannot manufacture the replacement and stored water is finite.
Hub water deliveries can extend the deadline but impose continuing expense and the risk that caravans reveal the Vault's location.

articleSections.title: Two missions
paragraphs: The first mission seeks a compatible chip, initially using Vault 15 as the lead. After its return, the Overseer sends the Dweller against the source of an artificially produced mutant army.

articleSections.title: Conditional failure states
paragraphs: If the water deadline expires, the population dies from deprivation. If Unity locates the Vault, super mutants invade. These are mutually exclusive failure branches, not events that occur on the successful route.

entities.summary: A guarded, irrigated and mostly self-sufficient settlement led by Aradesh, connected to Vault 15 through Katrina but not proven by Fallout alone to have an entirely Vault 15-derived founding population.
entities.description: Shady Sands combines subsistence agriculture, local medicine, raider pressure and conditional futures that range from NCR emergence to destruction.

articleSections.title: Settlement and economy
paragraphs: Shady Sands maintains gardens, a well, irrigation and brahmin while relying on barter and scavenging. Guards and an inward-looking leadership protect a community vulnerable to radscorpions and raiders.

articleSections.title: Vault 15 connection and its limits
paragraphs: Katrina is a Vault 15 survivor who lives in Shady Sands. Jarvis says an ancestor of Aradesh founded the settlement, but does not identify that founder's origin.
Fallout therefore establishes a migration connection without establishing the later, broader claim that every founder descended from Vault 15.

articleSections.title: Radscorpions and Khans
paragraphs: Radscorpions threaten residents and livestock; Razlo studies their poison. The Khans create a second crisis by abducting Tandi, drawing the Vault Dweller into a method-variable rescue.

articleSections.title: Conditional futures
paragraphs: The most favourable ending has Aradesh and Tandi guide Shady Sands into the New California Republic. Other branches remove either leader, place Tandi in sole authority, produce a council followed by raider destruction, or end in mutant invasion.
The NCR origin is therefore a Fallout ending possibility. Later continuity can select and elaborate a branch, but it should not make every Fallout ending simultaneous.

entities.summary: A multi-district trade centre built around caravan companies, water distribution, policing, organised crime and sharp inequality.
entities.description: The Hub connects regional commerce to the Unity plot: what begins as a missing-caravan mystery becomes evidence of captive screening and forced conversion.

articleSections.title: Districts and inequality
paragraphs: Downtown forms the caravan and merchant core. The Heights are affluent, Old Town is poor, and the Water Merchants operate to the south. This social geography underlies Loxley's redistributive claims and Decker's protection network.

articleSections.title: Water and caravans
paragraphs: Water Merchants control the main supply and can contract deliveries to Vault 13. Crimson Caravan and Far Go Traders connect settlements across dangerous routes, while caps circulate as Hub-backed money in Katrina's account.

articleSections.title: Missing caravans and Unity
paragraphs: Three Far Go caravans disappear in a month. Mutant Transmissions reveals that Unity scavengers capture travellers, assess contamination and forward viable people to the Lieutenant for processing at Mariposa.

articleSections.title: Crime, policing and Harold
paragraphs: Decker's Underground operates from the Maltese Falcon through extortion and killings; Justin Greene can act against it. Loxley leads a competing thieves' organisation in Old Town.
Harold supplies the city's deeper historical connection to Richard Grey and Mariposa, while his possible ending links personal treatment to a more egalitarian Hub.

articleSections.title: Conditional endings
paragraphs: One ending connects kindness toward Harold to a more equal Hub. A mutant advance causes residents to disperse in another. Many neutral state combinations receive no slide and should not be converted into invented outcomes.

entities.summary: The bombed ruins of Los Angeles, containing Adytum, the Blades, Followers, Gun Runners, deathclaw territory and the Cathedral complex.
entities.description: The Boneyard is a network of communities rather than a single government, with political, industrial, humanitarian and religious organisations occupying distinct sites.

articleSections.title: Angel's Boneyard and Los Angeles
paragraphs: Fallout dialogue explicitly equates Angel's Boneyard with the ruins of Los Angeles. Adytum, the Blades, Followers Library and Gun Runners factory form a connected but politically fragmented region.

articleSections.title: Adytum and Regulator control
paragraphs: Jon Zimmerman is the public leader, but the Regulators hold coercive power. Caleb's internal transmission proves he ordered Josh Zimmerman's murder and a frame-up of the Blades.

articleSections.title: Gun Runners and deathclaws
paragraphs: Gun Runners manufacture arms at a fixed industrial site and depend on Adytum materials after exhausting local scrap. A reproducing deathclaw nest blocks access and makes relocation difficult.

articleSections.title: Followers and Cathedral investigation
paragraphs: Nicole's Followers preserve knowledge, advocate peace and investigate the Children. Laura's infiltration ties the Boneyard's humanitarian network to the concealed Unity structure beneath the Cathedral.

entities.summary: The real-world dam on the Colorado River that became the focus of conflict between the NCR and Caesar's Legion.
The post-War city centred on the preserved Las Vegas Strip and ruled by Robert House.
The post-War Mojave region containing New Vegas, Hoover Dam and numerous competing communities.
A group of bunkers in the Mojave used by the local Brotherhood chapter.
The offshore installation that served as the Enclave's headquarters until its destruction in 2242.
A Vault near Boston built around a rehabilitation programme that Vault-Tec deliberately sabotaged.
The global nuclear exchange of 23 October 2077 that destroyed pre-War civilisation and abruptly transformed the Mariposa rebellion into a struggle for survival.
entities.description: For this cluster, the Great War is presented through its direct consequences at Mariposa: loss of communications, uncertainty about nearby strikes, sheltering families and the decision to abandon the base.

articleSections.title: Mariposa on 23 October 2077
paragraphs: Maxson's diary records the nuclear exchange from inside Mariposa. The garrison lost contact while questioning Leon von Felden and inferred that the original West Tek research centre had been struck. Mariposa itself was not hit in the opening exchange.
Because the soldiers had moved their families into the facility two days earlier, the base acted as a shelter through the first hours of the disaster.

articleSections.title: Immediate aftermath
paragraphs: The survivors did not know the wider scale of the destruction or whether fallout would reach them. Sergeant Platner's power-armoured survey on 25 October found no dangerous local atmospheric contamination at that time.

The absence of an immediate radiological barrier made evacuation possible, but it did not restore any external command. Maxson's group had to act on local information and pre-War contingency infrastructure.

articleSections.title: Consequence for the founding group
paragraphs: Before the bombs, the Mariposa crisis was a mutiny and secession. After them, the same personnel were responsible for soldiers, families, equipment and survival without any functioning national authority.

The exodus to Lost Hills and the later Brotherhood identity were not automatic consequences of nuclear war, but the war removed the institutions to which the garrison might otherwise have answered and made a new political and organisational settlement necessary.

entities.summary: The October 2077 collapse of command at Mariposa after soldiers discovered human FEV experiments, culminating in executions and Roger Maxson's secession from the United States.
entities.description: The rebellion was a sequence rather than a single moment: discovery, attempted restraint, interrogations, killings, Spindel's death and formal secession unfolded between 10 and 20 October.

articleSections.title: Cause
paragraphs: The security unit learned that Mariposa's scientists were experimenting on military prisoners with FEV. The discovery produced anger against the research staff and a breakdown in confidence in Colonel Spindel's command.

articleSections.title: Escalation and executions
paragraphs: Maxson initially stopped a soldier from killing a scientist and ordered interrogations. The process became lethal when he killed Robert Anderson on 13 October. After Spindel's suicide on 15 October, Maxson's authority hardened and the remaining interrogations ended in executions.

articleSections.title: Secession and outcome
paragraphs: Maxson declared the garrison seceded from the United States on 20 October, partly to force official attention onto Mariposa. No response arrived. The Great War followed three days later, and the rebels became the nucleus of the group that left for Lost Hills.

entities.summary: The 27 October 2077 departure of Mariposa's military personnel and families under Roger Maxson for the Lost Hills security bunker.
entities.description: The exodus carried the human community that would form the Brotherhood away from the site of the FEV experiments and into the post-War wasteland.

articleSections.title: Orders and departure
paragraphs: Maxson's 24 October order directed all military personnel and their families to depart for Lost Hills, drawing survival equipment from the base. His diary dates the actual departure to 27 October, after an atmospheric survey and the burial of the scientists.

articleSections.title: A military and civilian community
paragraphs: The column was not simply a combat unit. It included officers' and enlisted families, making protection, supplies and destination capacity central to the journey. Later records remember casualties among the less-protected civilians.

articleSections.title: Lost Hills and the Allen split
paragraphs: Lost Hills was the ordered destination and became the survivors' new home. During the movement, Sergeant Dennis Allen led a dissenting group away to search the irradiated West Tek ruins for technology, against Maxson's warning.

entities.displayName: Formation of the Brotherhood of Steel
entities.summary: The early post-War transformation of Maxson's Lost Hills community into a new order with its own name, ranks, traditions and mission.
entities.description: Released material establishes the sequence and ideas of the founding more securely than a single exact date. The archive therefore treats formation as a process culminating around 2082, not as an invented day-long ceremony.

articleSections.title: Preconditions
paragraphs: The founders had already broken with the United States, survived the Great War and established a home at Lost Hills. These events created an independent community, but Maxson believed shelter and old Army discipline were not enough to sustain it.

articleSections.title: The Brotherhood proclamation
paragraphs: In a broadcast preserved in Appalachia, Maxson proposed a Brotherhood of Steel: a new institution that would retain useful inheritance from the old world while refusing to restore the failed authority of the old United States.

articleSections.title: Ranks, traditions and mission
paragraphs: The new vocabulary of Elders, Knights and Scribes was intended to create belonging and purpose. A later address made the preservation of technical knowledge a central responsibility, with Scribes maintaining the archive and Knights protecting it.

entities.summary: The Vault Dweller's 2161 expedition to obtain a replacement water chip for Vault 13.
The destruction of the Master's immediate plans and military centres in 2162.
The formal establishment of the New California Republic in 2189.

entities.displayName: Destruction of the Enclave Oil Rig
entities.summary: The destruction of the Enclave's offshore headquarters in 2242.
The 2277 battle in which NCR forces stopped Caesar's Legion at Hoover Dam.
The climactic 2281 confrontation over Hoover Dam; its outcome varies with player choice.
A family of engineered viral agents developed from the Pan-Immunity Virion programme and redirected toward forced genetic alteration before the Great War.
entities.description: FEV is both a technology and a history of changing research aims. The early records move from disease resistance, through animal mutation experiments, to a classified military programme prepared for human testing at Mariposa.

articleSections.title: Pan-Immunity Virion origins
paragraphs: The programme began on 15 September 2073 as an American response to biological warfare. Its original objective was to alter uninfected DNA so that ordinary viral infection could no longer take hold.

This origin is important because the early programme was framed as protection from disease, not as a project to create transformed soldiers. The later FEV programme emerged when mutation and growth were treated as desirable rather than incidental effects.

articleSections.title: Renaming and animal tests
paragraphs: A West Tek experiment log dated 21 March 2075 records batch 10-011 being renamed Forced Evolutionary Virus. Early trials reported unusual resistance to infection and radiation alongside a new quad-helix structure.

Later entries document growth, aggression, altered intelligence and heritable effects across several animal species. The results were promising to the military programme but also showed that the agent's consequences could not be reduced to simple immunity.

articleSections.title: Transfer to Mariposa
paragraphs: On 7 January 2077 Major Barnett ordered all FEV research transferred to Mariposa. The scientist recording the order opposed human trials. Another programme summary describes the intended subjects as military volunteers, while Maxson's diary later identifies the people actually used as military prisoners.
Those descriptions are preserved with their source context. The archive does not let the programme's administrative language overwrite the garrison's discovery of coerced human experimentation.

articleSections.title: FEV and the Mariposa crisis
paragraphs: The human experiments triggered the security unit's revolt. The scientists said that government orders authorised the work; Maxson initially rejected that explanation, then accepted it only after the research staff had been killed.

FEV therefore shaped the Brotherhood before technology preservation became its formal mission. The founding experience was not merely that powerful technology existed, but that secret institutions could use it without meaningful accountability.

articleSections.title: Post-War legacy
paragraphs: Mariposa FEV later became associated with the Unity and the creation of super mutants. That later history transformed the programme from a founding trauma in Brotherhood memory into a continuing post-War threat.

Different FEV strains and programmes should not be assumed to be interchangeable. This record provides the shared subject and early chronology; future content passes can add strain-specific assertions and disputes without rewriting the origin story.

articleSections.title: Source notes and terminology
paragraphs: Fallout's FEV research summary and experiment disk provide the dated programme sequence. Maxson's diary provides the security unit's discovery and reaction. These sources answer different questions and should be read together.

The records sometimes describe the research as a programme and sometimes the engineered agent itself. The entity represents the broader FEV subject, while programme milestones remain separate event entities so that searches and timelines can distinguish institutional decisions from biological properties.

articleSections.title: Transmission and transformation
paragraphs: ZAX describes the tested agent as requiring injection or direct contact rather than airborne spread. It rewrites damaged or intact DNA with outcomes that depend heavily on the subject.

articleSections.title: Radiation and outcome quality
paragraphs: The scientific records connect radiation-damaged genomes with failed or poor transformations. The Lieutenant reaches a similar practical conclusion through a different, disputed explanation about wasteland exposure.

articleSections.title: Sterility evidence and limits
paragraphs: Vree directly observes atrophied reproductive anatomy and no viable sperm in examined mutants. ZAX's proposed gamete-repair mechanism is explicitly conjectural, while the Lieutenant calls sterility temporary.
The archive therefore distinguishes anatomical evidence, causal hypothesis and contradicted operational claim.

entities.summary: The United States Army colonel who commanded Mariposa's security detachment until the discovery of the FEV experiments precipitated his breakdown and death.
entities.description: Spindel's collapse left Roger Maxson, previously his second in command, as the effective leader of the Mariposa soldiers.

articleSections.title: Command at Mariposa
paragraphs: Spindel commanded the soldiers assigned to secure the classified research base. Maxson's diary depicts him becoming unresponsive as the personnel learned that military prisoners were being used in experiments.

entities.summary: A United States military officer whose January 2077 order transferred the FEV programme to Mariposa for its next phase.
The chief scientist at Mariposa, killed by Roger Maxson during an interrogation on 13 October 2077.
A Mariposa research scientist identified in Maxson's diary as the last member of the research staff to withstand interrogation before being killed.
A Mariposa scientist under interrogation when the Great War severed the base's external communications on 23 October 2077.
A member of the Mariposa security detachment who surveyed conditions outside the base in power armour on 25 October 2077.
A sergeant who broke from Maxson's survivors to lead an expedition into the irradiated West Tek ruins, later known as the Glow.
The commander of Taggerdy's Thunder who re-established contact with Roger Maxson after the Great War and organised the Appalachian Brotherhood under his remote guidance.
entities.description: Recordings between Taggerdy and Maxson preserve the earliest detailed explanations of the Brotherhood's name, ranks and preservation mission.

articleSections.title: Contact with Maxson
paragraphs: Taggerdy knew Maxson from their pre-War military service. When long-distance contact was restored, she accepted him as the senior surviving officer and brought her unit into the organisation he was developing at Lost Hills.

entities.summary: A pre-War research organisation whose Pan-Immunity Virion work developed into the FEV programme before the research was transferred to Mariposa.
entities.description: The original West Tek research installation became the irradiated site later called the Glow; the organisation and the place are represented separately so programme responsibility is not confused with geography.

articleSections.title: The FEV programme
paragraphs: West Tek's work began with disease resistance and moved toward forced genetic alteration. Its surviving experiment records provide the dated transition from PIV to FEV and document escalating animal trials before the military ordered the programme moved to Mariposa.

entities.summary: The West Tek research programme established in 2073 to seek broad immunity from biological attack and later developed into the FEV programme.
The United States Army unit assigned to guard Mariposa, including Robert Spindel, Roger Maxson and personnel whose families sheltered at the base.
entities.description: Its transition from security unit to rebel garrison, refugee column and institutional ancestor of the Brotherhood is modelled as changing relationships rather than a single timeless identity.

entities.summary: An Army Ranger unit led by Elizabeth Taggerdy that survived in Appalachia and became the organisational nucleus of the Appalachian Brotherhood.
The early Appalachian chapter formed from Taggerdy's Thunder through long-distance contact with Roger Maxson and Lost Hills.
The early Brotherhood division of responsibilities among elders and the Paladin, Knight and Scribe traditions.
Maxson's programme for recovering, protecting and extending technical knowledge so it could support future civilisation.
The pre-War state and broad post-War region containing Mariposa, Lost Hills and much of the early western Brotherhood's history.
The irradiated ruins of the original West Tek research installation, later explored by Dennis Allen's breakaway expedition.
entities.description: The Glow is both a lethal post-War ruin and the archive that preserves West Tek's research history through ZAX, laboratories and holodisks.

articleSections.title: The West Tek research facility
paragraphs: Before the Great War the site hosted biological work alongside physics, laser and power-armour programmes. ZAX records initialization in 2053, biological research from 2055 and military control from 2071.

articleSections.title: PIV and FEV evidence
paragraphs: ZAX and recovered disks trace cure research into PIV and FEV, escalating animal trials and the January 2077 transfer to Mariposa. The records distinguish established observations from ZAX's own conjectures.

articleSections.title: Brotherhood expeditions
paragraphs: Dennis Allen's expedition reached the irradiated ruins and lost members to radiation and security systems despite power armour. In 2161 Cabbot uses the same destination as an outsider initiation task.

entities.summary: The formal establishment of the West Tek PIV programme on 15 September 2073 in response to biological-warfare threats.
The 21 March 2075 West Tek milestone at which experimental batch 10-011 was redesignated as Forced Evolutionary Virus.
Major Barnett's 7 January 2077 order moving all FEV research to Mariposa for the next stage of the programme.

Sergeant Platner's 25 October 2077 power-armoured reconnaissance outside Mariposa after the nuclear exchange.
The 26 October 2077 burial of the research staff killed during the Mariposa rebellion.
The late-2077 arrival of Maxson's Mariposa survivors at the Lost Hills bunker, remembered as the establishment of their new home.
Roger Maxson's death from cancer in 2135, after which leadership passed to the next Maxson generation.
An addictive chem whose origin is represented by conflicting and source-dependent evidence.
A family of powered combat armour developed before the Great War and closely associated with several military factions.
The control component whose failure prompted Vault 13 to send the Vault Dweller into the wasteland.
The unnamed official who sends the Vault Dweller to solve the water crisis, assigns the mission against the mutant source and ultimately refuses the returning hero readmission.
entities.description: The Overseer frames both central missions and the final political choice to preserve Vault 13's closed society by excluding the person who saved it.

articleSections.title: The water-chip mission
paragraphs: When Vault 13's purification controller fails, the Overseer concludes that the Vault cannot manufacture a replacement before its stored water is exhausted. He sends one resident toward Vault 15, the nearest known lead for a compatible chip.
Water shipments from the Hub can delay the crisis, but they do not repair the system and may expose the Vault through repeated caravan traffic.

articleSections.title: The mutant-source mission
paragraphs: After the replacement chip is returned, the Overseer presents evidence that the unusual mutants threatening the region are being deliberately produced. The second mission is to neutralise that source.
The successful main route requires both Mariposa's vats and the Master beneath the Cathedral to be removed, but their order and the method used are player-dependent.

articleSections.title: Exile after victory
paragraphs: On the Vault Dweller's return, the Overseer acknowledges the scale of the achievement but still bars the hero from Vault 13. His stated concern is that younger residents will imitate the Dweller and abandon the community.
Exile is common to the successful ending variants. The player may leave or kill the Overseer, so his survival belongs to a conditional outcome rather than fixed history.

entities.summary: A Vault east of Vault 13 whose post-War crowding, scarcity, schism and later attack are remembered by Katrina.
entities.description: Fallout connects Vault 15 to Shady Sands through Katrina but does not establish that every founder of Shady Sands came from the Vault.

articleSections.title: The pre-War record
paragraphs: Vault Locations v34.129 places Vault 15 due east of Vault 13 and advertises a reinforced third level. Like the same record's claims for other Vaults, this is promotional material rather than a complete operational history.

articleSections.title: Crowding and schism
paragraphs: Katrina remembers being raised amid severe crowding and inadequate equipment. A schism divided the population, and a departing group took much of the best equipment.
Her recollection is first-person evidence but includes admitted gaps after injury; the archive preserves it as testimony rather than omniscient history.

articleSections.title: Connection to Shady Sands
paragraphs: After a later attack on Vault 15, Katrina eventually settled in Shady Sands. Jarvis separately says an ancestor of Aradesh founded the settlement, without naming that founder's origin.
Together the sources prove a Vault 15 migrant connection, not the broader claim that the entire settlement was founded by Vault 15 descendants.

entities.summary: The Garl-led raider group that kidnaps Tandi and threatens Shady Sands in 2161.
entities.description: The Khans are a local organised raider faction. Garl's claims about succession and trade are retained as his self-presentation rather than silently promoted to neutral fact.

articleSections.title: Garl's raiders
paragraphs: Garl Death-Hand leads the group from a wasteland camp near Shady Sands. He presents violent strength as a basis of authority and claims to have taken leadership by killing his father.

articleSections.title: Kidnapping of Tandi
paragraphs: The Khans abduct Tandi from Shady Sands. Her release can follow payment, intimidation, combat or a personal challenge, so no single rescue method is canonical to Fallout.

articleSections.title: Possible futures
paragraphs: Ending narration allows the raiders to be destroyed or dispersed, regroup and continue terrorising the region, or raid north until the mutant army destroys them. These branches are mutually exclusive.

entities.summary: A guarded trading town divided between Killian Darkwater's civic authority, Gizmo's casino patronage and the Skulz gang.
entities.description: Junktown's central conflict is a struggle over law, commerce and organised crime rather than a simple good-versus-evil tableau.

articleSections.title: Civic authority and commerce
paragraphs: Killian Darkwater combines mayoral authority with ownership of the general store, while Lars commands the town guards. Their authority is visible but contested by Gizmo's wealth and criminal network.

articleSections.title: Gizmo's assassination plot
paragraphs: Gizmo owns the casino and arranges an attempt on Killian's life. Evidence can be recorded and delivered to Lars, or the Vault Dweller can support Gizmo instead.
Because the confrontation is player-dependent, the archive records the plot as an initial condition and groups the possible civic results separately.

articleSections.title: Gangs, medicine and companions
paragraphs: The Skulz operate around local drinking establishments and perform work linked to Gizmo. Sherry's possible defection shows gang affiliation is changeable. Doc Morbid's clinic can be exposed as part of an illicit trade in human remains.
Tycho and Dogmeat provide two different routes into the town's social history: one through a travelling Ranger tradition, the other through Phil's account of a previous owner killed by Gizmo's men.

articleSections.title: Conditional endings
paragraphs: Under Killian, one ending depicts Junktown as safe and fair under strict frontier justice. A Gizmo victory produces rapid commercial growth that later chokes the town. Mutant invasion destroys it in a third branch.

entities.summary: The Hub merchant house controlling the city's principal water source and able to deliver temporary water supplies to Vault 13.
A high-risk Hub caravan company led by Demetre Romara and formerly employing Ian as a guard.
A Hub trading company whose caravan disappearances expose the Unity's captive-processing network.
Decker and Kane's Maltese Falcon-based protection, extortion and contract-killing network in the Hub.
The ghoul settlement in the ruins of Bakersfield, divided between Set's surface rule, an underground community and Unity occupation of the Watershed.
entities.description: Necropolis is a layered polity and infrastructure crisis: Set can govern surface ghouls while Unity controls the strategic water facility and peaceful ghouls depend on a damaged pump below.

articleSections.title: Bakersfield and Vault 12
paragraphs: Fallout explicitly identifies Necropolis with Bakersfield. Vault 12 lies beneath the ruins and contains a high-capacity purification system capable of processing sewer water.
The Fallout 1 Vault Locations record does not describe a deliberate open-door experiment. That later claim remains outside the game's evidence scope.

articleSections.title: Set and Unity occupation
paragraphs: Set rules the surface population and portrays himself as a sovereign spared by the Master. At the same time, Unity mutants occupy the Watershed and Harry captures normal humans under orders from a commander he calls Lou.
The evidence supports layered control: Set retains local authority under coercive limits, while Unity controls infrastructure and military activity.

articleSections.title: The water system
paragraphs: Peaceful ghouls shelter in the sewers and depend on a broken pump. A compatible control chip can be removed from Vault 12's system, making repair of the pump decisive for the settlement's possible future.

articleSections.title: Mutually exclusive outcomes
paragraphs: If the chip is removed without repairing the pump, one ending has Necropolis die of dehydration. Repair permits an engineering and trade recovery. A mutant-invasion override destroys the settlement, although refuge dialogue leaves exact survivor numbers uncertain.

entities.summary: The Vault beneath Bakersfield whose purification system supplies the setting for Necropolis's water crisis and the replacement chip.
A Boneyard agricultural community publicly led by Jon Zimmerman but coercively controlled by Caleb's Regulators.
Caleb's armed organisation controlling Adytum and proven by its own transmission to have murdered Josh Zimmerman and framed the Blades.
Razor's community of castoffs west of Adytum, blamed for Josh Zimmerman's death but able to expose and resist the Regulators.
Gabriel's industrial community manufacturing weapons and ammunition while dependent on Adytum materials and blocked by deathclaws.
The Children of the Cathedral's public church and the access layer above the Master's concealed command Vault.
entities.description: The Cathedral joins public relief work, coercive religious organisation, covert Nightkin security and the Master's command centre in one layered site.

articleSections.title: Public church and headquarters
paragraphs: The Children use the Cathedral as their principal religious headquarters while operating hospitals and missions elsewhere. Morpheus leads the public hierarchy and Lasher's dialogue exposes an internal doctrine of pain and obedience.

articleSections.title: The concealed Vault
paragraphs: A hidden Vault beneath the church contains the Master's command centre. Laura's infiltration and Nightkin guards reveal the separation between the public institution and Unity's protected inner structure.

articleSections.title: Confrontation and destruction
paragraphs: The Master can be defeated through persuasion, combat or access to a nuclear device. Successful ending narration records destruction of the command centre, but does not select one method as canonical.

entities.summary: A religious and medical movement preaching peace and Unity while secretly serving the Master's coercive programme.
entities.description: The Children are neither identical with the mutant army nor independent of it: they provide a public humanitarian face, recruitment network and access structure for Unity.

articleSections.title: Public mission
paragraphs: The Children offer hospitals, healing and a theology that promises peace through Unity. Their reach across southern settlements makes them the movement's most visible human institution.

articleSections.title: Coercion and hierarchy
paragraphs: Morpheus presents himself as a senior partner of the Master, while Lasher treats pain and enforced obedience as legitimate discipline. The Lieutenant instead describes Morpheus as a useful but disposable recruit.

articleSections.title: Followers investigation
paragraphs: Nicole suspects the Children after dissidents disappear. Laura infiltrates the Cathedral and confirms protected access, while Nightkin use concealed areas behind the public church.

entities.summary: The composite mutant intelligence leading the Unity, strongly identified through converging Fallout evidence with the transformed expedition leader Richard Grey.
entities.description: The Master's anti-war diagnosis is joined to forced biological assimilation: suitable humans are converted, others sterilised or killed, and uncontaminated Vault populations treated as raw material.

articleSections.title: Richard Grey and Mariposa
paragraphs: Harold's testimony and Richard Grey's audio diary describe the same Mariposa expedition and vat accident. Grey survives, changes through assimilation, experiments further and conceives Unity.
No located Fallout line simply states that Richard Grey is the Master. The archive therefore models one identity while marking the bridge as a strong editorial inference backed by convergent sources.

articleSections.title: The Unity plan
paragraphs: The Master argues that human difference caused war and that one mutant race can end conflict. The operational programme is compulsory: suitable humans are converted, compliant non-converts face sterilisation and resistance is eliminated.
Vault residents matter because minimally contaminated subjects produce better transformation results.

articleSections.title: The sterility challenge
paragraphs: When confronted with evidence that super mutants cannot reproduce, the Master initially appeals to FEV-2's design and demands proof. Vree's anatomical observations and the broader scientific record undermine the plan's future.
Persuasion can lead him to accept failure and initiate destruction, but combat and a nuclear route remain alternative player-dependent methods.

entities.summary: The senior Unity commander at Mariposa who supervises conversion, interrogation, captive processing and the search for Vault populations.
entities.description: The Lieutenant is authoritative about Unity policy but not necessarily about FEV science; his explanations of sterility and wastelander transformation conflict with other evidence.

articleSections.title: Command at Mariposa
paragraphs: The Lieutenant commands the Military Base's mutant forces, detention areas and conversion vats. Unity field reports send screened caravan captives to him for processing.

articleSections.title: The search for prime normals
paragraphs: He describes uncontaminated Vault residents as ideal conversion subjects and treats consent as irrelevant. This makes the discovery of Vault 13 an existential failure state for its population.

articleSections.title: Contested FEV explanations
paragraphs: The Lieutenant attributes poor transformations to wasteland radiation or altered FEV exposure and dismisses sterility as a temporary production problem. ZAX describes damaged DNA causing unstable outcomes, while Vree directly observes reproductive failure.
The archive preserves the Lieutenant's statements as claims rather than merging them into the scientific model.

entities.summary: Humans transformed through FEV exposure whose strength, cognition, disfigurement and reproductive capacity vary with subject and process.
entities.description: Fallout supplies strong evidence for transformation and reproductive impairment, but it does not justify one universal molecular mechanism for every mutant.

articleSections.title: Transformation by FEV
paragraphs: Direct FEV exposure rewrites genetic material. Viable subjects may gain muscle and cognitive capacity, while others experience organ failure, disfigurement, memory loss or death.
The Master's programme favours low-contamination Vault subjects because damaged wastelander genomes produce less predictable results.

articleSections.title: Reproductive evidence
paragraphs: Vree reports atrophied reproductive organs and no viable sperm in examined bodies. ZAX separately labels a gamete-repair explanation conjectural.
The specimens strongly support reproductive impairment; precise cause and universality remain less certain.

articleSections.title: Role in Unity
paragraphs: Unity uses super mutants as soldiers, guards and commanders. Individual intelligence and authority vary substantially, from Harry at the Watershed to the Lieutenant at Mariposa.

entities.summary: An elite stealth-equipped grouping of super mutants trusted with concealed Unity and Cathedral duties.
entities.description: Fallout does not supply a formal biological taxonomy separating Nightkin as a species; the archive models them as a subgroup or role within super mutants.

West Tek's 2055 establishment of biological research seeking cures for the New Plague.

disputes.assessment: Myron claims responsibility for Jet, while later released material is commonly read as placing Jet in a pre-War context. The records are shown separately because their scope, narrator reliability and chronology do not support a silent single-answer resolution.

Fallout establishes that Katrina left Vault 15 and lived at Shady Sands, while Jarvis names an ancestor of Aradesh as founder without identifying that person's origin. A wholly Vault 15-derived founding population is not established by Fallout alone.

The diary chronology and transformation sequence make the Richard Grey–Master identity a strong inference, but the archive preserves the distinction between cumulative evidence and an explicit single-source identity statement.
Morpheus presents himself as the Master's partner; the Lieutenant's language places him lower and treats him as expendable. Both source statements remain visible.

Vree reports direct anatomical observations; ZAX offers a conjectural mechanism; the Lieutenant calls the problem temporary. These differ in evidentiary status and should not be collapsed into one claim.
Both sources associate contaminated subjects with poorer conversion, but their explanations and authority differ. ZAX reports experimental observations; the Lieutenant supplies an operational theory.
The cautious-aid and Steel Plague slides are opposed branches. Neither should be presented as an unconditional description of the Brotherhood.
Dehydration, restored survival and mutant invasion are conditional outcomes produced by different world states.
